options: Re-checking trust signals throughout a session, not just once at initial login
Verifying a user's identity exactly once, permanently, at account creation
A setting that disables MFA after the first successful sign-in
A method for encrypting data at rest continuously
questions.explain: Continuous verification means trust signals like device compliance and risk level are re-checked throughout a session, not just accepted once at sign-in.

questions.q: How does Conditional Access implement Zero Trust's "verify explicitly" tenet?
options: By re-evaluating its conditions, such as requiring MFA, on every single access attempt rather than once at login
By disabling all authentication checks after the first sign-in
By applying the same MFA requirement to every sign-in with no conditional logic
By only checking identity once per calendar month
questions.explain: Conditional Access policies are evaluated continuously, for as long as a user is active, which is what makes them a real implementation of verify explicitly.

questions.q: In the example where a user's managed laptop fails a compliance check 20 minutes into a session, what happens?
options: The next access attempt can be challenged or blocked, since the device-compliance condition no longer holds — without a new sign-in
Nothing happens until the user manually logs out and back in
The session is immediately and permanently terminated with no recovery option
Conditional Access ignores device compliance after the initial sign-in
questions.explain: Because Conditional Access re-evaluates conditions on every access attempt, a mid-session compliance change can trigger a block or remediation request immediately.

questions.q: Which Zero Trust tenet does requiring a compliant device, as a Conditional Access control, put into action?
options: Least privilege access — access isn't handed to just any device that has the right password
Assume breach, exclusively, with no connection to least privilege
None — device compliance has no connection to Zero Trust tenets
Verify explicitly only, with no relation to privilege at all
questions.explain: Requiring a compliant device limits access to devices that meet a standard, which is least privilege access in practice.

questions.q: Why does Conditional Access being evaluated on every access attempt matter, compared to a one-time login check?
options: It allows the system to react to signals that change mid-session, like a sign-in's risk level or a device's compliance status, without waiting for logout
It has no practical benefit over a one-time check
It only matters for users who sign in from mobile devices
It replaces the need for MFA entirely
questions.explain: A one-time login check can't react to anything that changes afterward; continuous, per-request evaluation is what lets Conditional Access catch a mid-session change in risk or compliance.
